result.topic_en: Euler finds the pressure at any point of the second tube section, fixes the constant C by continuity at F, sets the pressure at the outlet CD equal to atmospheric pressure, and solves for the height due to the outflow velocity.
result.transcription:
348 TENTAMEN THEORIAE
cuius valor in quouis puncto medio euaneſcit, in puncto autem D, vbi ſubito eſt $z=b$, et $s=b$, erit
$4\int\frac{e^{\alpha r}dz}{z^5}=e^{\frac{\alpha b}{f}}\left(\frac{1}{f^4}-\frac{1}{b^4}\right)$
29. In quouis ergo puncto intermedio M erit preſſio
$p=Ce^{\frac{-\alpha s}{f}}+\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha s}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta$
et quia, poſito $s=0$, preſſio in F prodit $=C$, neceſſe eſt, vt ſit $C=le^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}+\frac{g}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}\right)+b^4v\left(\frac{1}{g^4}-\frac{1}{f^4}\right)$
Quo valore notato orietur preſſio in extremo orificio
CD$=Ce^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}+\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta+b^4v\left(\frac{1}{f^4}-\frac{1}{b^4}\right)$
30. Quoniam hic vero aqua in aërem erumpit, aliam preſſionem non ſuſtinet, praeter pondus atmoſphaerae, vnde erit,
$l=Ce^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}+\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta+b^4v\left(\frac{1}{f^4}-\frac{1}{b^4}\right)$
et ſubſtituto valore ipſius C habebitur
$l=le^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}-\frac{\alpha b}{f}}+\frac{g}{\alpha}e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}\right)+e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}b^4v\left(\frac{1}{g^4}-\frac{1}{f^4}\right)$
$+\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta+b^4v\left(\frac{1}{f^4}-\frac{1}{b^4}\right).$
31 Ex hac iam aequatione celeritas eruitur, qua aqua per orificium CD erumpit. Pprodibit enim alti-
huic celeritati debita
$v=\frac{l\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}-\frac{\alpha b}{b}}\right)-\frac{g}{\alpha}e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}\right)-\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta}{e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\cdot\frac{b^4}{g^4}+\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\right)\frac{b^4}{f^4}-1}$

In quouis ergo puncto intermedio M erit preſſio
$p=Ce^{\frac{-\alpha s}{f}}+\frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha s}{f}}\right)\mathrm{coſ.}\,\zeta$
items.english: Therefore at any intermediate point M the pressure will be p = C e^{-αs/f} + (f/α)(1 − e^{-αs/f}) cos ζ.

items.quote: et quia, poſito $s=0$, preſſio in F prodit $=C$, neceſſe eſt, vt ſit $C=le^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}+\frac{g}{\alpha}\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}\right)+b^4v\left(\frac{1}{g^4}-\frac{1}{f^4}\right)$
items.english: And since, putting s = 0, the pressure at F comes out = C, it is necessary that C = l e^{-αa/g} + (g/α)(1 − e^{-αa/g}) + b^4 v(1/g^4 − 1/f^4).

items.quote: Quoniam hic vero aqua in aërem erumpit, aliam preſſionem non ſuſtinet, praeter pondus atmoſphaerae
items.english: But since here the water bursts out into the air, it sustains no other pressure than the weight of the atmosphere.

items.quote: Ex hac iam aequatione celeritas eruitur, qua aqua per orificium CD erumpit.
items.english: From this equation the velocity with which the water bursts out through the orifice CD is now found.
